newsitem.title: UK: UK water lobby group warns on European directives.
newsitem.headline: UK water lobby group warns on European directives.

text.p: A lobby group for British water customers warned on Wednesday the cost of implementing proposed new European directives on bathing and drinking water could mean an extra 20 stg on average household water bills.

The National Customer Council of industry watchdog Ofwat (ONCC) said in a statement that revised directives, "if adopted, could together put 20 stg or nine percent on the average household water and sewerage bill."
It called on the European Parliament to consider water customers' interests in relation to costs and affordability when it votes on the revisions.
The European Parliament is meeting on Wednesday to discuss the proposed revisions, ONCC said.

"We are not opposed to higher quality standards but we must ensure that the European Union...does not overlook the pressing questions of the willingness and ability of customers to pay," ONCC chairman Jim Gardner said.
The proposed revisions include tighter controls on lead content in drinking water and on the presence of bacteria from human and animal faeces in bathing water.
ONCC calculated that directives on lead could cost around two billion stg in England and Wales while those on bathing water could mean costs of 4.2 billion stg.
